profile.reading:
Sabey Data Centers operates the Intergate.Columbia campus at 4405 Grant Road in East Wenatchee, Douglas County, Washington, along the Columbia River in central Washington state. Sabey Corporation was founded in 1972 by Dave Sabey as a Pacific Northwest commercial real estate developer, and the company entered the data center business around 2010 when a large tenant vacated a Seattle building during the dot-com era downturn, leaving behind space that became SDC Seattle Building 5. Sabey Data Centers was formally established that same year as a partnership between Sabey Corporation and institutional investor National Real Estate Advisors. The company's own site currently lists seven operating campuses, SDC Ashburn, SDC Austin, SDC Columbia, SDC Manhattan, SDC Quincy, SDC Seattle, and SDC Umatilla, together totaling more than 3.5 million square feet, with additional projects described by the company as in development.

Per Sabey's own SDC Columbia campus page, the East Wenatchee site runs on hydroelectric power supplied by Douglas County Public Utility District, priced at 5 cents per kilowatt hour, among the lowest electricity rates available to data center operators anywhere in the country. Douglas County PUD draws its hydroelectric generation from Columbia River dams the utility operates, the same regional low-cost hydropower base that has also drawn data center investment to nearby Quincy and other mid-Columbia sites operated by other companies. The Intergate.Columbia campus comprises three completed buildings and a fourth under construction, with 70 megawatts currently under power campus-wide and, per the operator, more than 90 additional megawatts of capacity coming as buildout continues, a total Sabey does not break down building by building. Sabey markets the campus at an average annualized power usage effectiveness of about 1.2, and states its ENERGY STAR score has consistently ranked in the 95th to 100th percentile among comparable buildings, most recently a 99 for 2024. The campus holds ISO 27001 certification, SSAE 18 SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 attestations, and is described by the operator as HIPAA, HITECH, and PCI DSS compliant, with connections to more than seven Tier 1 network carriers including AT&T, Verizon, Charter Spectrum, Zayo, and Ziply Fiber. Sabey describes the facility's reliability design as Tier III standard equivalent, backed by 2.75 megawatt backup generators rated for 72 hours of runtime.

No building-specific street address distinct from the shared campus address at 4405 Grant Road has been located for Intergate.Columbia D. Sabey's own campus page describes a fourth building currently under construction at the Columbia campus, consistent with Building D being the most recently added structure on this site, though this record does not assert that identification as confirmed by the operator by name. No building-specific megawatt or square footage figure has been published by the operator for Building D alone, only the campus-wide totals above.
profile.capacity_note: not published at the building level. Campus wide total is 70 MW (operator figure), not applied to this individual building. Baxtel separately notes 9 MW of additional Tier III capacity expected campus wide from Q4 2026, a future figure not applied to critical_it_mw.

profile.campus_power_note: Per Sabey's own SDC Columbia page (fetched 2026-09-06), the Intergate.Columbia campus is served by Douglas County Public Utility District hydroelectric power priced at 5 cents per kWh, with 70 MW currently under power campus-wide across three completed buildings and a fourth under construction, and more than 90 additional MW described by the operator as coming. reading.body:
Intergate.Columbia D is one building on the Sabey Data Centers campus in East Wenatchee, Washington, which sits on Douglas County Public Utility District hydroelectric power at 5 cents per kilowatt hour. The campus as a whole operates 70 megawatts across three completed buildings and a fourth under construction, with the operator stating more than 90 additional megawatts coming, though Sabey publishes no breakdown of load by individual building. At a typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, the entire campus's current 70 megawatts would accommodate roughly 1,750 racks. Building D itself may be the fourth structure currently under construction, but the operator has not published a building-specific power figure or square footage for it.

The site qualifies to host HIPAA-regulated workloads under HITECH compliance, payment card data under PCI DSS, and ISO 27001 certified systems. The campus holds SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 attestations and claims ENERGY STAR scores in the 95th to 100th percentile, most recently 99 for 2024. Tier III design is backed by 2.75 megawatts of backup generation rated for 72 hours of runtime.

This campus ranks third by published megawatt capacity in Washington state, behind only two other mapped facilities that have disclosed figures. The state has 46 mapped data center facilities total, but only three publish power specifications, leaving Intergate.Columbia as part of a very small set of disclosed large loads. Whether Building D matters to AI scaling depends on its actual IT load and the pace at which Sabey brings the operator's stated 90-plus additional megawatts online, neither of which is published.
